history.summary: CSV town 'Nagaur' is approximate: Mundiyar is a village ~2.5 km from Nagaur town (per the IGNCA/ASI documentation format report RJ/NGR-127), postal PIN 341028. The ASI-IGNCA report documents a large 15th-century Jain temple complex there ('khandar' - partly ruined), with highly ornate doors, lintels, foliated columns, foliated arches, and a main shrine with a domical superstructure whose ribbed-pattern dome with inverted lotus and cresting is described as a masterpiece; the interior is highly decorated with floral motifs. Note a conflict: the same IGNCA coordinates are given as LONG 75 deg 15' E, LAT 27 deg 40' N, which lies far east of Nagaur and contradicts the stated '2.5 km from Nagaur' approach note - treat the IGNCA coordinates as unreliable and the village-location approach note as authoritative (verify). Also in Mundiyar village is the well-known Mundal Mata Mandir (a Hindu temple, rated ~4.7-4.8 on Justdial) - the two are distinct sites. No web photographs of the Jain khandar could be found, so media is intentionally empty.

name: Mundiyar Jain Temple
town_description: Mundiyar is a small village a few kilometres from Nagaur town in Nagaur district, best known locally for the Mundal Mata Mandir; the ASI-documented 15th-century Jain temple complex (khandar) stands here as well.

travel.airport: Jodhpur Airport is the nearest major airport (~140 km - verify); Jaipur International Airport is ~250 km away.
travel.railway: Nagaur railway station is the nearest railhead (~2.5-5 km from the village - verify).
travel.road: The village is ~2.5 km from Nagaur town on the Nagaur side and is connected by regular bus services (per IGNCA).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; cool desert-winter season is most comfortable.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented (the site is partly ruined - verify access before visiting). Media intentionally empty: no reliable photograph of this khandar found online.
